MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  DECEMBER 11, 2018

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR HUFF at 6:30 p.m. and the City Council convened into closed session in the City
Manager’s Office, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates.

City Council Members Present: Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent: Mitchell

City Staff Present: City Manager Douglas R. Prichard
  City Attorney Donald M. Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis

CLOSED SESSION (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER)

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1); United States District Court Case No. 2:18-cv-
  10011-R-MAAx; Cherie Townsend, et al v. Los Angeles County, et al.

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

  ***
Mayor Huff adjourned the Closed Session portion of the meeting at 7:10 p.m.

At 7:16 p.m., MAYOR HUFF called the meeting back to order in open session in the City Council
Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, CA.

  ***
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

A group of government students from Palos Verdes Peninsula High School led the Pledge of
Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  Mitchell

City Staff Present: City Manager Douglas R. Prichard
  Assistant City Manager, Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Donald M. Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
DECEMBER 11, 2018
   Planning Director David Wahba
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Analyst Jessica Slawson
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT “RECYCLING HERO” DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR’S FREE
  RESIDENTIAL REFUSE SERVICE –4TH QUARTER 2018

  Winning entries: Arlene Lewis, Rollingwood Drive (Residential) and Masuda
  Investments, Silver Spur (Commercial)

B.  RESOLUTION OF COMMENDATION – KRISTIE BISHOP, RETIRING ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES EMPLOYEE

  MAYOR HUFF presented a Resolution of Commendation to Kristie Bishop in recognition
  of her retirement from the City of Rolling Hills Estates after 35 years of service to the City

C.  PRESENTATION TO OUTGOING MAYOR BRITT HUFF

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN recognized MAYOR HUFF for her service to the City
  of Rolling Hills Estates and introduced those present to make presentations to her.

  Assembly Member Al Muratsuchi thanked MAYOR HUFF for her service to the
  community and presented her with framed certificate of appreciation in recognition of her
  term as Mayor.

  On behalf of Senator Ben Allen, Olina Winbroe thanked MAYOR HUFF for being a partner
  with Senator Allen’s office and for her tireless with work in the City and South Bay. She
  presented her with a certificate of appreciation in recognition of her term as Mayor.

  On behalf of Supervisor Janice Hahn, Erika Velasquez thanked MAYOR HUFF for her
  service and dedication to the City of Rolling Hills Estates and presented her with County
  Resolution in recognition of her term as Mayor.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN thanked MAYOR HUFF for her service to the City of
  Rolling Hills Estates as Mayor and reviewed the many accomplishments during her 2017-
  18 term as Mayor. He expressed appreciation to MAYOR HUFF for her service to the
  City and presented her with a commemorative gavel in recognition of her term as Mayor.

  MAYOR HUFF noted her appreciation for the comments and thanked the COUNCIL and
  staff for a great year.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
DECEMBER 11, 2018
 CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of
  the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown
  by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on
  separately.)

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS A-H AS
  PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL ADJOURNED MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 27, 2018

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

C.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 27, 2018

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

D.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – NOVEMBER AND DECEMBER 2018

  APPROVED WARRANTS 60820 THROUGH 60849 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $300,898.60; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 110118 THROUGH 110818;
  59843 (VOID); 60594 (VOID); 60693 THROUGH 60705; 60758 THROUGH
  60773; 60793 THROUGH 60810 IN THE AMOUNT OF $343,502.06 FOR A
  GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $644,400.66.

E.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 19, 2018

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 26, 2018

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
DECEMBER 11, 2018
 G.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION – WORK PERFORMED BY ALL AMERICAN ASPHALT FOR
  THE 2018-19 STREET RESURFACING PROJECT

  1) ACCEPTED THE 2018-19 STREET RESURFACING PROJECT AS
  COMPLETE; 2) AUTHORIZED THE CITY CLERK TO FILE A NOTICE OF
  COMPLETION FOR THE PROJECT WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  REGISTRAR-RECORDER’S OFFICE; AND 3) IF NO CLAIMS ARE FILED
  WITHIN 35 DAYS AFTER RECORDATION, DIRECTED STAFF TO RELEASE
  THE 5% CONSTRUCTION RETENTION PAYMENT TO ALL AMERICAN
  ASPHALT IN THE AMOUNT TO $41,242.97

H.  SEMI-ANNUAL CODE COMPLIANCE REPORT – JUNE 1, 2018 THROUGH
  DECEMBER 1, 2018

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

  OUTGOING MAYOR HUFF thanked COUNCIL and staff for their support over the last year
  and recognized staff’s involvement in the major projects and objectives that were
  undertaken over the last year. She commented that is has been an honor to serve as Mayor
  and noted that one of the highlights of the last year has been the opportunity to connect with
  more residents at the various community events including the Holiday Parade and during
  the 2018 election. She stressed the importance of continuing to focus on emergency
  preparedness, public safety and addressing the needs of the City’s aging population. She
  also thanked her husband for his unwavering support during her term as Mayor.

  MAYOR HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN

  TO APPOINT JUDY MITCHEL TO SERVE AS MAYOR

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

  COUNCIL MEMBER  ZERUNYAN  moved,  seconded  by  COUNCIL  MEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN

  TO APPOINT VELVETH SCHMITZ TO SERVE AS MAYOR PRO TEM BY
  ACCLAMATION.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, THE COUNCIL SO ORDERED.

  ***

  At 7:55 p.m. MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting to a brief reception.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ called the meeting back to order at 8:13 p.m.

  ***

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
DECEMBER 11, 2018
 PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Angie Gilbride of California Water Service Company provided an update on the status of the Palos
Verdes Peninsula Water Reliability Project.

Martin Gombert, Administrator, Palos Verdes Peninsula Transit Authority, announced that PV
Transit will offer free dial-a-ride shuttle service to Peninsula residents from 6:00 p.m.-2:00 a.m. on
New Year’s Eve/New Year’s Day and reservations can be made beginning December 20. He
further noted that an advertisement will be broadcast on Channel 33 and brochures explaining the
service will be available to the public.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

NEW BUSINESS

A.  WESTFIELD PROPERTY OWNERS ASSOCIATION CAMERA GRAN REQUEST

  Recommendation: That the City Council confirm the existing requirement that grants be
  offered only to HOAs and neighborhoods located in Rolling Hills Estates and deny the
  request of the Westfield POA.

  Administrative Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ called for comments from the public.

  Vatche Shirikjian and Fred Tramm, residents of the Westfield Neighborhood, addressed
  the COUNCIL regarding their $1,500 grant request and commented they believe that the
  camera would not only benefit the Westfield Neighborhood, but the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates as well and would help the Lomita Sheriff’s Station in solving crimes.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN asked for clarification with regard to the location, height
  and other characteristics of the camera. Mr. Tramm responded to the inquiry and
  explained that the camera points toward the Westfield neighborhood entrance.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that the question for the requestors, form
  a policy standpoint, is what is different about this request compared to a neighboring
  community that may make a similar request in the future.

  In response to COUNCL MEMBER ZERUNYAN, Mr. Shirikjian stated that is about
  assisting the Lomita Sheriff’s Station in solving crime and it is a greater community project
  to promote safety. Mr. Framn noted that this is also an opportunity to assess a different
  camera as an additional tool to provide an added layer of security.

  Tony Trutanich expressed concern that the cameras would also be monitoring innocent
  people.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
DECEMBER 11, 2018
   COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN thank the applicant and staff for their work on this
  project and commented that he is supportive of approving this request because it provides
  benefit to more than just the Westfield entryway.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF concurred with COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN’S
  comments.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that the argument he found compelling
  was that approving this grant request will provide an opportunity to asses an additional
  type of camera through a pilot program; but he is not willing to change the policy in
  general.

  City Attorney Davis commented that earlier today Sgt. Gaw of the Los Angeles County
  Sheriff’s Department raised an issue with regard to Civil Code Procedures that govern
  ALPR cameral installations pertaining to record keeping and access to the records. He
  suggested that the matter be tabled to allow additional time to review and address these
  issues.

  Following discussion, COUNCIL tabled consideration of this matter to allow the City
  Attorney time to research the issues raised.

OLD BUSINESS

A.  PILOT PROGRAM (NEIGHBORHOOD ENTRYWAY SECURITY CAMERA)

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the one-year Pilot Program for the
  Montecillo neighborhood with the appropriate budget adjustment in the amount of $1,600
  and direct staff to enter into a contract with FLOCK to establish the Pilot Program in
  partnership with the Sheriff’s Department’s Technology and Support Division subject to
  final review by the City Attorney.

  Administrative Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  In response the COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, Administrative Analyst Slawson clarified that
  the camera would be on one-year lease with the option to renew for additional years at a
  cost of $2,000 at the HOA’s expense.

  Discussion ensued concerning the data to be collected by the camera and the
  functionality of the camera itself.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ suggested that the agreement contain language that
  should the HOA discontinue the contract, the Sheriff’s Department, as the custodian of
  records, should retain the data and it should not be returned to FLOCK.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
DECEMBER 11, 2018
   COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by, COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE ONE-YEAR PILOT PROGRAM FOR
  THE MONTECILLO NEIGHBORHOOD WITH THE APPROPRIATE BUDGET
  ADJUSTMENT IN THE AMOUNT OF $1,600 AND DIRECT STAFF TO ENTER
  INTO A CONTRACT WITH FLOCK TO ESTABLISH THE PILOT PROGRAM IN
  PARTNERSHIP WITH THE SHERIFF’S DEPARTMENT’S TECHNOLOGY AND
  SUPPORT DIVISION SUBJECT TO FINAL REVIEW BY THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell

CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to other
  Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of currently active Council Committees,
  ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers
  authorities and their various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or have an interest,
  which are not otherwise agendized.

A.  COMPREHENSIVE ANNUAL FINANCIAL REPORT AND RELATED DOCUMENTS FOR
  FISCAL YEAR ENDED JUNE 30, 2018

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file the Comprehensive Annual
  Financial Report (CAFR) for fiscal year ended June 30, 2018.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN commented that there were no issues raised by the
  auditor that need to be brought to the COUNCIL’S attention. He noted that the City’s
  current auditor will not be doing the City’s audit moving forward and the City will need to
  retain a new audit firm.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ expressed appreciation to the auditor and staff for their
  efforts in producing the audit.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by, COUNCILMEMBER
  ZERUNYAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE COMPRESSIVE ANNUAL
  FINANCE REPORT FOR FISCAL YEAR ENDED JUNE 30, 2019.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
DECEMBER 11, 2018
 MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to request information
  on currently pending projects and/or issues of public concern, direct that an item be
  agendized for future consideration and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

A.  COMMISSION & COMMITTEE APPOINTMENTS

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ reported that the COUNCIL recently conducted a recruitment
  for openings on various Commissions and Committees and was fortunate to have had
  several well qualified applicants. She expressed her appreciation to all of the participants
  and thanked thank everyone for their participation in the process and willingness to serve
  on these important Commissions and Committees. She stated upon completing the
  interviews the COUNCIL concurred in making the following appointments:

    Park & Activities Commission – Judy Bain and Ryan McCormick
    Environmental Advisory Committee – Robert Bacinski and Navi Uppal
    Traffic & Safety Committee – John Martin

OTHER MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN provided an update on the upcoming Clean Power Alliance
Board meeting including the discussions related to rate setting and timing.

COUNCILMEMBER HUFF reported that the Metro Board recently approved the C-3 realignment
option as supported by Supervisor Janice Hahn.

COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN thanked COUNCILMEMBER HUFF and staff for a successful
holiday parade.

COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that he has received comments from members of
the public expressing concerning regarding the urgent care medical use facility recently
approved by the Planning Commission at the Peninsula Center. He suggested that the matter
(PA-21-18) be brought before the City Council for discussion related to policy.

  PLANNING APPLICATION PA-21-18 WAS CALLED UP FOR PUBLIC HEARING
  BEFORE THE COUNCIL.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ reminded everyone about the City’s annual holiday ADOPT-A-
FAMILY program and encouraged participation.

CLOSED SESSION (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER – SEE ABOVE)

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  8
DECEMBER 11, 2018
 ADJOURNMENT

At 9:23 p.m. MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ adjourned the City Council meeting in memory of
former United States President George H.W. Bush. The next regular meeting of the City Council
will be held on Tuesday, January 8, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills
Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Douglas R. Prichard
City Clerk  City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  9
DECEMBER 11, 2018
